title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Let \hat\pi_{0,3} be the profinite fundamental group of P^1-{0,1,\infty}. It is free profinite on two generators, with inertia generators l_0, l_1, l_\infty and l_0 l_1 l_\infty = 1. It sits as a normal subgroup of index 6 in \hat{\mathfrak S}^+_{0,3}, with quotient S_3. This ambient group has topological generators \sigma_\infty (order 2) and \rho (order 3), and defining relations \sigma_\infty^2 = (g\rho)^3 = 1. It is therefore Z/2 * Z/3 profinitely completed, i.e. \hat{PSL_2(Z)}. Geometrically it is the orbifold fundamental group of the lambda-line divided by S_3, which is the j-line.

The previous page proves a theorem. Outer 'star' automorphisms of \hat\pi_{0,3} (those preserving the inertia conjugacy classes) that commute with S_3 correspond uniquely to automorphisms u of \hat{PSL_2(Z)} such that:
- u fixes \sigma_\infty;
- u(\rho) = g\rho with g in \hat\pi_{0,3};
- u preserves the conjugacy class of L_0 = <l_0>.
Such a u is encoded by two pieces of data:
- a multiplier p in \hat Z^*, with \gamma = (p-1)/2;
- a class g_0 in \hat\pi_{0,3}/L_0.
From g_0 one forms h_0 = \sigma_\infty(g_0)^{-1} g_0. The data must satisfy the 3-cycle relation (48): \xi \rho(\xi) \rho^2(\xi) = 1, where \xi = l_0^\gamma h_0^{-1}. This is equivalent to (g\rho)^3 = 1, with g = \sigma_\infty(g_0 l_0^\gamma) \rho(g_0)^{-1}.

What this page does.
(36) It restates u: \sigma_\infty \mapsto \sigma_\infty and \rho \mapsto g\rho.
(49) It computes the effect of u on the three inertia generators: u(l_i) = int(g_i)(l_i^p), with
- g_1 = g\rho(g_0) = \sigma_\infty(g_0) l_1^\gamma = \sigma_\infty(g_0 l_0^\gamma);
- g_\infty = g\rho(g_1) = g\rho(g)\rho^2(g_0) = \rho^2(g^{-1}g_0), where the last step uses (38) g\rho(g)\rho^2(g) = 1;
- g_\infty is also rewritten as \rho(g_0 l_0^\gamma) h_0 (modulo L_\infty).
These follow by transporting l_0 via \sigma_\infty and \rho, using that S_3 permutes the inertia classes.

Dictionary with Drinfeld's GT. Since \sigma_\infty(h_0) = h_0^{-1}, the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1 is built in: h_0 is written as a \sigma_\infty-coboundary. Relation (48), with exponent \gamma = (p-1)/2, is exactly Drinfeld's hexagon (3-cycle) relation. The pair (p, h_0) is thus the (\lambda, f) of \hat{GT}_0, i.e. GT without the pentagon.

Crossed-out corollary. It considers a second homomorphism \hat\varphi: \hat\pi_{0,3} \to \hat{\mathcal O}^*_{0,3}, defined up to outer equivalence by l_0 \mapsto \sigma_\infty\rho, l_1 \mapsto \sigma_\infty, l_\infty \mapsto \rho^{-1}. This is the orbifold quotient map. It arises from viewing the j-line itself as P^1 minus three points carrying orbifold orders (\infty, 2, 3). Grothendieck asks when u commutes with \hat\varphi, so that the same automorphism data acts compatibly on both pictures:
- the lambda-line as an index-6 subgroup of \hat{PSL_2(Z)};
- the j-line coordinate, giving \hat\pi_{0,3} as surjecting onto \hat{PSL_2(Z)}.
His criterion is twofold:
- existence of \beta in \hat Z with \varepsilon_1^{-\beta} h_0 \varepsilon_0^\beta = \sigma_\infty(\hat\varphi(h_0))^{-1}\hat\varphi(h_0) (29);
- equivalently, existence of \alpha with h_0^{-1} l_1^\gamma \rho = int(\varepsilon_0^\alpha \hat\varphi(\rho^{-1}h_0))(\rho^\beta) (30), where necessarily \alpha = \beta + \gamma.
The margin adds that \beta is unique and \alpha is determined. The whole corollary is struck through with 'cf plus loin'.

The next page reinterprets solutions \xi of the 3-cycle equation as splittings of the extension of Z/3 by \hat\pi_{0,3}, i.e. as order-3 elements over \rho, with \hat\pi_{0,3} acting by twisted conjugation.
errors: The ambiguous notation (rho used both for the order-3 element and, in the transcription, for the multiplier) makes the page hard to read. In (49) the exponent on l_i is the multiplier p (\gamma=(p-1)/2), not the later \beta of the corollary.
The expression g_\infty = \rho(g_0 l_0^\gamma) h_0 is only meaningful modulo L_\infty (g_i are defined up to right multiplication by L_i). I did not verify it fully; it is plausible but unchecked.

The corollary is crossed out. Its claimed equivalence (29) <=> (30) and the assertion \alpha=\beta+\gamma are not proved on the page. The well-definedness of \hat\varphi (which is only exterior: l_0'l_1'l_\infty' is not literally 1 as written) is glossed over.

ideas.what: Outer S_3-equivariant inertia-preserving automorphisms of \hat\pi_{0,3} realized as automorphisms of \hat{PSL_2(Z)}=Z/2*Z/3 fixing \sigma_\infty and sending \rho to g\rho; formulas for the induced action on the inertia generators l_0, l_1, l_\infty.
ideas.modern_name: \hat{GT}_0 (GT without pentagon) acting on \hat F_2 and \hat{PSL_2(Z)} / \hat B_3 mod center
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the 'jeu de Lego-Teichmüller' and the role of genus 0, 3-4 points, but not these explicit formulas

ideas.what: Writing f=h_0=\sigma_\infty(g_0)^{-1}g_0 as a coboundary (so the 2-cycle relation is automatic) and the 3-cycle relation \xi\rho(\xi)\rho^2(\xi)=1 with exponent (p-1)/2.
ideas.modern_name: Drinfeld's relations (I) and (II) for (\lambda,f); f=g(y,x)^{-1}g(x,y) parametrization

ideas.what: Compatibility condition of the automorphism u with the orbifold quotient map \hat\pi_{0,3} -> \hat{PSL_2(Z)} given by the j-line viewed as P^1 with points of orders (\infty,2,3).
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of GT action with the (2,3,\infty) triangle-group / j-line uniformization (lambda-line vs j-line)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; related themes in Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura on GT and M_{1,1}

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates (then strikes out, deferring 'plus loin') an explicit criterion for when a GT_0-type automorphism of \hat\pi_{0,3} is compatible with the second description of \hat{PSL_2(Z)}. In that description, the j-line itself is a P^1 minus three points with orbifold orders (\infty,2,3). The criterion is the existence of \beta (and \alpha=\beta+\gamma) satisfying (29)/(30). For Galois elements this compatibility holds automatically. For abstract GT elements it is a self-similarity condition that could cut out a subgroup or might follow from the pentagon. I do not know of an explicit treatment of exactly this 'lambda-line vs j-line' consistency equation in the GT literature.
missed.quote: Pour que l'homom. (18) \hat\varphi : \hat\pi_{0,3} \to \hat{\mathcal O}^*_{0,3} défini extérieurement par l_0 \mapsto \sigma_\infty\rho, l_1 \mapsto \sigma_\infty, l_\infty \mapsto \rho^{-1}, commute à u, il faut et il suffit que [l'on] puisse trouver \beta \in \hat{\mathbb Z} ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Natural candidate relation for GT (or for GT_0) coming from the self-similarity P^1-{0,1,\infty} -> j-line. Deciding whether it is implied by Drinfeld's relations or defines a proper subgroup would be relevant to the question of whether GT^ equals G_Q.

missed.claim: Independent, pre-Drinfeld derivation of the hexagon relation with exponent (p-1)/2. The 2-cycle relation is encoded by writing f as a \sigma_\infty-coboundary, and the 3-cycle relation as an order-3 element of \hat{PSL_2(Z)}. This gives documentary evidence of Grothendieck's priority for the 'two-and-three-cycle' part of GT.
missed.quote: u(l_0)= int(g_0) l_0^{p}, u(l_1) = int(g_1) l_1^{p} = int(\sigma_\infty(g_0))(l_1^{p}), u(l_\infty) = int(g_\infty)(l_\infty^{p})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: the content is known (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak-Schneps), but its explicit appearance in Grothendieck's ~1981 notes is not generally documented.

deep.surprise_reason: The main content (GT_0 relations via automorphisms of \hat{PSL_2(Z)}) is well known since Drinfeld, Ihara and Lochak-Schneps, though here it is explicit and pre-Drinfeld. The crossed-out compatibility criterion with the j-line orbifold map is a modestly interesting, apparently unpursued thread.
transcription_corrections: In (49) the exponents are l_i^{p} (the multiplier, written like a superscript p/\rho in the image), not l_i^{\beta}; \beta first appears in the corollary.
'commute à \Gamma [?] : u [?]' should read roughly 'commute à u' ('commutant à u').
'il faut et il suffit que puisse trouver' should read 'il faut et il suffit que l'on puisse trouver'; 'on a qui revient à' should read 'ou ce qui revient au même'.
The heading is 'Corollaire' and the whole corollary block, including (29) and (30), is struck through by large diagonal lines.
Left margin reads approximately 'Cf plus loin pour plus [?]' and '\beta unique ! \alpha [?] uniquement déterminé'.
